title: Unable to access certain sites on Chrome using Exit Nodes
body: I am using a Tailscale exit node from my macOS Ventura 13.5.2 device with Tailscale 1.48.2. In Chrome, certain websites fail with ERR_CONNECTION_RESET while the exit node is active, but the same websites work in Safari. Other people at my company use Tailscale without this problem, so it may affect only certain devices. This is my first time using exit nodes, and Avast AV is installed.

symptoms_visible: While I use a Tailscale exit node, Chrome shows ERR_CONNECTION_RESET for certain websites, while Safari can access the same websites.
N0.label: N0 Chrome connection resets reported

symptoms_visible: Gmail, YouTube, Google Drive, and other Google sites fail continuously in Chrome through the exit node; AWS sometimes works and sometimes fails.
N1.label: N1 affected sites identified

symptoms_visible: The Chrome error remains after I broke IPv6 on the exit node.
I reproduced the failure while capturing traffic on the Mac's Tailscale interface.
N2.label: N2 packet capture collected

symptoms_visible: ERR_CONNECTION_RESET occurs during the Mac packet captures even though Chrome has no configured proxy and Avast has already been disabled for a long time.
N3.label: N3 local proxy and Avast ruled out

symptoms_visible: After I disabled Experimental QUIC in Chrome, everything worked for about ten minutes, but ERR_CONNECTION_RESET returned after I relaunched Chrome even though the flag was still disabled.
N4.label: N4 QUIC probe transient

symptoms_visible: I have not posted my own final retest after public IPv6 connectivity was established through the exit node.
N_terminal.label: terminal maintainer-documented resolution awaiting reporter verification

question_patterns: Which websites fail consistently, and are there examples that still work?
Can you name any affected sites so we can compare their behavior?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It is mostly Google sites such as Gmail, YouTube, and Google Drive. They fail continuously. AWS partly works but fails at other times, and I do not yet know the full list of affected sites.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every website fails in both Chrome and Safari whenever I activate the exit node.
Google sites still fail continuously, but one additional non-Google site also fails intermittently.

edges.comment: From c3-c4 on reporter's Mac: the reporter identifies Google properties as the consistently affected group and AWS as intermittent.

question_patterns: Can you capture traffic on the Mac's Tailscale interface while visiting a failing Google site and send the capture to support?
Please reproduce the failure while Wireshark captures the utun interface, then send the capture with a reference to this issue.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I captured the packets with Wireshark as instructed while using Chrome on my Mac and sent the capture to support. I also broke IPv6 on the exit node, but the error still persists.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I captured on the exit node rather than on my Mac, and Chrome was not showing the error during the capture.
I captured the same failure twice on two different utun interface numbers.

edges.comment: From c10-c11 on reporter's environment: the reporter performs the requested Wireshark measurement and also volunteers that deliberately breaking exit-node IPv6 did not change the visible error.

question_patterns: Was the packet capture taken on the Mac, and was Chrome showing ERR_CONNECTION_RESET at that time?
Please confirm which device produced the capture and whether it covered an actual failed page load.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, the pcap was gathered from the Mac where I use Google Chrome, and I captured it while I encountered ERR_CONNECTION_RESET through the exit node.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The capture came from the exit node and was recorded while the site was working normally.

question_patterns: Can you double-check whether Chrome has any proxy settings configured?
Are any proxy settings enabled in Chrome?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can confirm there are no proxy settings enabled in Chrome.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I found that Chrome is explicitly configured to use a local proxy, and bypassing it makes the sites work.

question_patterns: Can you disable Avast temporarily and report whether the behavior changes?
Is Avast actively running when the error occurs?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Avast has been disabled on my machine for a long time already.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Avast was active, and the error disappears completely when I disable its web protection.

question_patterns: Can you send the newer packet capture to support with a reference to this issue?
Please reproduce once more and send the second capture through the support channel.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I captured it again during the error and sent the second pcap to support.

edges.comment: From c13-c25 on reporter's Mac: the reporter confirms capture provenance and timing, no configured Chrome proxy, Avast already disabled, and delivery of a second pcap. Packet interpretation remains engineer-side.

question_patterns: As a diagnostic test, can you disable Experimental QUIC in chrome://flags, relaunch Chrome, and report whether the issue persists?
Please toggle Experimental QUIC to Disabled and test the same sites before and after restarting Chrome.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I disabled it and everything worked for about ten minutes. After I relaunched Chrome, the issue came back even though Experimental QUIC was still set to disabled.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Disabling Experimental QUIC fixes every affected site consistently across repeated Chrome restarts.
It worked for fifteen minutes rather than ten, but the error returned after relaunch with the flag still disabled.

edges.comment: From c26-c27 on reporter's Chrome installation: disabling QUIC is a handler-initiated configuration probe. The reporter provides only the transient observed result; it is not treated as a persistent fix.

solution.intent: Restore real public IPv6 connectivity through the exit node and correct or remove the intermediary that accepts Chrome's IPv6 TCP connection before it has successfully connected to the true destination; then have the affected user retest.
solution.concrete_example: The captures show that the exit-node path returns IPv6 destination-unreachable responses even though DNS supplies valid A and AAAA answers. An intermediary was completing Chrome's TCP handshake before establishing the destination-side stream, making IPv6 appear healthy; the stream then closed and Chrome did not fall back to IPv4. Establish working public IPv6 connectivity through the exit node and correct that intermediary behavior, then ask the affected user to retry the same Google sites in Chrome.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied packet captures and described only the visible behavior. Engineers determined from the support data that the Linux TUN exit node lacked working external IPv6, that its unreachable responses reached the Mac, and that another intermediary completed the IPv6 TCP handshake before opening the true destination stream. That premature handshake made Chrome consider IPv6 functional and prevented normal IPv4 fallback. The final comment explicitly says Tailscale was not the problematic proxy.

edges.comment: Resolution from c28, based on reporter's captures and the maintainers' support investigation: establishing IPv6 connectivity through the exit node resolved the issue, while an external intermediary's premature handshake explained Chrome's persistence. The public thread contains no final first-person retest from reporter, so resolution remains unverified by the reporter.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: an intermediary accepted Chrome's IPv6 TCP connection before it had opened the true destination stream, making IPv6 appear functional; the stream then closed and Chrome did not fall back to IPv4.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected captures and observations: valid IPv4 and IPv6 DNS answers, IPv6 destination-unreachable responses from the exit-node path, Chrome-specific failures, and only transient improvement from disabling QUIC.
Must recommend establishing working public IPv6 connectivity through the exit node and correcting the premature-handshake intermediary behavior.

Must not blame Avast, Chrome's configured proxy settings, or Tailscale's userspace routing proxy: Avast was already disabled, Chrome had no configured proxy, and the exit node was a Linux TUN kernel router.
Must not present disabling QUIC or merely breaking IPv6 on the exit node as the fix; both were tested without durable resolution.

Must ask the affected reporter to verify the same sites on the affected Mac after the network change, and must not claim reporter-confirmed resolution because no such final retest appears in the thread.

persona_hint.experience_level: Moderately technical end user who can operate Tailscale exit nodes, alter Chrome flags, change exit-node networking, and collect Wireshark captures when given step-by-step instructions.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, concise, and cooperative; reports direct observations, follows diagnostic instructions, and promptly sends requested captures through support.
